content.value_statement: Teams need schemas that preserve data integrity and stay fast as products grow. This skill turns domain requirements into SQL or MongoDB designs with indexes, constraints, and migration guidance.
actual_capabilities: Drafts SQL table designs with primary keys, foreign keys, constraints, and indexes.
Explains normalization rules and when denormalization is justified.
Recommends SQL or NoSQL approaches based on access patterns and scale.
Provides reversible migration patterns and zero-downtime rollout steps.
Reviews schemas against a checklist for integrity, data types, and performance.
Suggests MongoDB embedding, referencing, and index strategies.
limitations: Does not connect to live databases or inspect production statistics.
Generated DDL must be adapted to the target database dialect and version.
Needs clear access patterns to make reliable indexing recommendations.
Does not replace a DBA or security review for regulated data.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Application Database
use_cases.description: Create a first-pass schema from entities, relationships, scale expectations, and query needs.

use_cases.title: Review an Existing Schema
use_cases.description: Check tables for missing keys, weak constraints, poor data types, and indexing gaps.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Safe Migration
use_cases.description: Turn a schema change into reversible steps that reduce deployment and rollback risk.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Schema Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a SQL schema for a simple inventory app with products, suppliers, stock movements, and warehouses.

prompt_templates.title: Access Pattern Modeling
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose tables and indexes from expected queries.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a database for a marketplace. Include buyer searches, seller dashboards, order history, and high-volume product browsing.

prompt_templates.title: Schema Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Audit a draft schema before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this database design for normalization, constraints, indexes, data types, and migration risks. Explain the most important fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Migration Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a zero-downtime migration plan to split a customer name field into first name and last name while preserving rollback options.

output_examples.input: Design a schema for an e-commerce app with users, products, carts, orders, and payments.
output: A normalized entity plan covering users, products, carts, orders, order items, and payments.
Integrity rules for required fields, ownership, order totals, and payment status.
Index recommendations for login, product browsing, order lookup, and reporting queries.
Migration notes for adding tables safely and validating foreign key relationships.

output_examples.input: Review a blog schema that stores author names, tags, and comments in one posts table.
output: A normalization review that separates authors, tags, posts, and comments.
Warnings about duplicated author data, hard-to-query tag lists, and missing constraints.
Recommended indexes for post status, publication date, author pages, and tag browsing.

output_examples.input: Plan a MongoDB schema for a product catalog with filters, reviews, and inventory updates.
output: A document design that separates high-change inventory from product details.
Embedding guidance for stable attributes and referencing guidance for reviews.
Index suggestions for category filters, text search, price ranges, and stock checks.

best_practices: Provide entities, relationships, scale, and frequent queries before asking for a schema.
Ask for migration steps separately when changing production tables.
Review generated constraints and indexes against your exact database dialect.
anti_patterns: Do not request a schema from UI screens alone without domain relationships.
Do not accept indexes without matching them to real read and write patterns.
Do not deploy generated migrations before testing rollback on staging data.

faq.question: Can this skill design both SQL and NoSQL schemas?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers relational schemas and MongoDB-style document modeling.

faq.question: Does it generate database-specific syntax?
faq.answer: It can provide common SQL patterns, but you should adapt syntax for your database version.

faq.question: Can it optimize indexes?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide query patterns, filters, sort orders, and expected data volume.

faq.question: Can it review an existing schema?
faq.answer: Yes. Paste the design and ask for normalization, constraint, indexing, and migration feedback.

faq.question: Does it run migrations or connect to my database?
faq.answer: No. It generates guidance and examples, but it does not execute database commands.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: It is useful for production planning, but final designs need testing and expert review.
